metadata.title: Copied Agreement: Lineage-Grounded Audits of Claim Preservation in Data Migration
metadata.description:
This record contains version 20 of Copied Agreement: Lineage-Grounded Audits of Claim Preservation in Data Migration, together with its complete technical supplement and supporting research artefact.

Equal outputs before and after a schema migration can reproduce a common error when the target is populated from an inadequate source. In a synthetic tax-jurisdiction migration of 1,728 records, comparing old and new flags finds 48 disagreements. Comparing both flags with separately recorded delivery evidence finds 74 affected records, including 26 where the flags agree and both are wrong. The proposed audit separates whether the available inputs determine the promised claim, whether endpoint results agree, and whether those results are supported by relevant evidence. Four checks on a declared production graph expose copying and shared dependencies. Counterexamples show why a passing graph check still cannot establish that an evaluator actually uses its independent evidence. A finite test diagnoses when ground values can be reconstructed from shared inputs; its limitations are explicit. For a fixed ground, two graph conditions compose across migration steps, while two require additional ancestry conditions or a fresh audit. Coq proofs support the core results and extracted OCaml checks. An executable walkthrough and a measured synthetic scaling experiment show how to apply the audit and where its cost grows. Positive assurance still requires adequate evaluators, faithful evidence, sufficient coverage, resolved concerns and accountable custody.

The archive includes the 28-page main article, the 50-page technical supplement, editable LaTeX sources, Coq and OCaml sources, reproduction instructions, retained verification records and SHA-256 checksums. The scaling study contains 54 configurations with five timed measurements each, giving 270 retained measurements.

The release is pinned to repository commit 0619413077a4cb85fcc67819ec776ce414085d29.
